question: Does one bounded public NASA report contain machine-extractable numerical measurements, rather than figure-only curves, that can test density-dependent film RMS granularity or NPS/MTF shape without fitting or stock claims?

source.title: Computer enhancement of radiographs
source.copyright: Work of the US Government; public use permitted according to the NTRS record

allowed_after_pass: freeze one no-fit comparison of an unchanged generic density-dependent grain amplitude primitive against extracted table values
retain aperture/MTF/PSD facts only as separated scanner-plus-film controls when explicitly tabulated
forbidden: digitize plots or infer values from raster/vector figure geometry
treat radiographic film as colour-negative or consumer-camera stock evidence
infer exposure, developer, scanner or process labels not printed in the report
fit P4 parameters during the source audit
redistribute source content as project fixtures

branch_rule.source_pass: Open one fixed no-fit generic density/granularity compatibility audit.
branch_rule.source_fail: Close this source without figure digitization and continue another ready algorithm or physical leaf.

claim_ceiling: Source-feasibility evidence from one public 1973 radiographic-film/scanner report; not camera-film stock, modern emulsion, colour, process, scanner calibration or product evidence.
